title: Minimum Swaps To Make Sequences Increasing
summary: Given two integer arrays, nums1 and nums2, of the same length, you can swap the elements at the same index in one operation.
statement: Given two integer arrays, nums1 and nums2, of the same length, you can swap the elements at the same index in one operation. The goal is to make both arrays strictly increasing. A strictly increasing array means each element is greater than the previous one. Determine the minimum number of such swaps required to achieve this condition.
constraints: Arrays have equal positive length and some swap set makes both strictly increasing.
At index i, swapping exchanges nums1[i] and nums2[i].
Return the minimum number of indices to swap.
hints: Track minimum costs ending with the current index kept or swapped.
Same-orientation inequalities extend like states; cross inequalities transition between states.
Compute both next costs from the previous pair.
Every solution has exactly one of two orientations at each index, and the valid transitions enumerate all possibilities.
editorial: Every solution has exactly one of two orientations at each index, and the valid transitions enumerate all possibilities.

tests.explanation: Swapping the final pair makes both arrays strictly increasing.
Swapping at index one is sufficient.
